title: Packet retention-failure memory remembers transient storage errors and serves them unmarked
outcome: A transient storage or I/O failure in the parent packet's terminal-attempt publication does not hide the attempt until the record changes, or the served error says it is remembered and how to retry.
acceptance: Either only deterministic publication failures (terminal cut changed, corrupt custody) are remembered and a transient storage error is retried on the next packet read, or a served remembered error is marked as remembered and names the explicit attempt-only read as the retry path. Shown by a behavioural test.
